description: Research Experiences for Undergraduates (REU), NSF NHERI 2025: Algorithmic Correction of Coastal Wind Measurements for Anemometer Tilt and Terrain Effects During Landfalling Hurricanes is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Priya Whitley, University of Connecticut (uconn.edu). This project entails the development and validation of an algorithm to correct deployable Sentinel weather station wind speed and direction measurements in hurricanes for mast vibration, sway, and tilt. Reusable corrected data can be used to improve hurricane modeling, enhance structural design codes, and support emergency planning. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project with 3 top-level files (PDF). Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-hav8-cc61. Keywords: Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel, University of Florida, Sentinel tower, Hurricane wind measurements, Anemometer tilt correction, Real-time correction algorithm. Published 2025-08-22. Facility named: Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel - University of Florida. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is CC-BY-4.0 (labelled "Creative Commons Attribution" on the DesignSafe project). Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
